conformance-contracts/contracts/stat-all:
schema_version = 1
id = "kernel.fs.stat-allocation"
title = "Warm regular-file fstat avoids host heap allocation"
guest_surfaces = ["syscall:fstat", "syscall:statx", "syscall:newfstatat"]
semantic_authority = ["Linux inode identity, file mode, ownership, timestamps and device-node stat semantics"]
fixture = "kernel-syscall-floor --allocation-check"
scale_points = [1, 8, 32, 128]
rationale = "Host-backed fstat needs scalar inode data, not copied path strings. Warm valid regular-file fstat must allocate zero host heap objects; cold inode-cache initialization and other fd kinds are outside this fixture. Metadata fallback values and description lock lifetime remain unchanged."

[bindings]
vm_free = "carrick-kernel-example::kernel-syscall-floor --features allocation-metrics --allocation-check"

[bindings.unresolved]
embed_structural = "Signed stat and metadata validation pending. Production allocation observation remains open."
docker = "Pinned Linux stat semantic authority binding pending."
promotion = "Uninstrumented paired syscall and workload performance acceptance pending."

[[structural_budgets]]
kind = "affine"
metric = "host_heap_allocations"
base = 0
per_unit = 0
layers = ["vm-free"]
rationale = "Warm regular-file fstat requires no host heap objects. Allocator events are observed only inside dispatch, with an independently verified positive control."
crates/carrick-kernel-example/Cargo.toml:
[package]
name = "carrick-kernel-example"
version.workspace = true
edition.workspace = true
license.workspace = true
description = "The bring-your-own-execution-backend template for carrick-kernel: a VM-less backend that runs scripted Linux tasks on host threads over Vec-backed guest memory."

[lib]
name = "carrick_kernel_example"
path = "src/lib.rs"

[lints]
workspace = true

[dependencies]
# carrick-kernel is taken with NO features: this crate is the
# bring-your-own-backend template, so its backend is its OWN impls
# (`ExampleProcess`, `ExampleStage1Projection`, `ExampleMmBackend` in
# `src/process.rs`) over the kernel's ordinary public surface -- which is the
# point. It uses none of the kernel's `test-support`-gated doubles, and taking
# the feature would have made the template quietly depend on a test surface a
# real backend author does not get.
carrick-kernel = { path = "../carrick-kernel" }
carrick-vfs = { path = "../carrick-vfs" }
# carrick-hal's `test-support` IS required, and only for the two Null bridges
# (`NullHostSignalBridge`, `NullGuestTimerBridge`), which are gated behind it so
# they are not linkable from a product build. Enabled through a NORMAL
# dependency, so resolver 2 unifies it into carrick-hal for every package built
# in the same selection as this crate. The product build is never that
# selection: the root manifest's `default-members` restricts an argument-less
# `cargo build --release` (scripts/build-signed.sh) to carrick-cli's closure,
# and `just check-layering` fails if that selection enables `test-support` on
# carrick-hal, carrick-kernel or carrick-vfs. A `--workspace` build (clippy,
# doc, test) does unify it, which is what lints and renders the gated surface.
carrick-hal = { path = "../carrick-hal", features = ["test-support"] }
carrick-guest-mem = { path = "../carrick-guest-mem" }
carrick-abi = { path = "../carrick-abi" }
carrick-observability = { path = "../carrick-observability" }
carrick-conformance-contract = { path = "../carrick-conformance-contract" }
parking_lot.workspace = true
serde_json.workspace = true
tempfile.workspace = true
thiserror.workspace = true

[features]
# Non-product allocation observation; never enabled for timing claims.
allocation-metrics = []
conformance-metrics = ["carrick-kernel/conformance-metrics", "carrick-observability/conformance-metrics"]

[dev-dependencies]
carrick-kernel = { path = "../carrick-kernel", features = ["conformance-metrics"] }
carrick-observability = { path = "../carrick-observability", features = ["conformance-metrics"] }
carrick-vfs = { path = "../carrick-vfs", features = ["test-support"] }
libc.workspace = true
tempfile.workspace = true
